purpose: Meclofenamate is used to relieve pain, reduce swelling and inflammation, and ease stiffness caused by conditions like arthritis. It can also help with mild to moderate pain and painful menstrual periods. Doctors may prescribe it when other pain relievers have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Meclofenamate works by blocking the enzymes that produce these chemicals, so you feel less pain and inflammation. Think of it like turning down the volume on your body's pain and swelling signals.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, heartburn, and gas. Some people also experience dizziness or headaches. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of heart attack, stroke, or serious stomach bleeding, especially if taken for a long time or in high doses. Do not take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Avoid it during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, kidney problems, high blood pressure, or a history of stomach ulcers. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 50 to 100 mg taken by mouth every 4 to 6 hours as needed, but no more than 400 mg per day. Always take it with food, milk, or antacids to protect your stomach. Follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition.
